Food culture


Evaluating food culture and nutrition science
Types of evidence and utility in establishing causal inference
Although the combined historical experience of various cultures on the optimal relationship between food, diets, and health is help-
ful by itself, it is insufﬁcient to determine whether relationships are valid or not. Single studies are inadequate to demonstrate cause-
effect relationships and it is important to consider not only the strength of studies, but the type and quality of the research available.
When many different types of evidence are supportive of a causal relationship, the weaknesses of individual studies are mitigated
and causal inference is strengthened. In determining the validity of food folklore or traditional and complementary medicine, not
only the totality of the evidence but also the type and quality of available evidence are important
